rol: ⭐ EL MOMENTO IRREPETIBLE. Centro de la sección 2 'WHAT'S INSIDE DECIDES', sobre la banda a sangre de crema #E4D7C0. La única imagen clara de una página oscura.
prompt: Photorealistic forensic close-up, dead-on and perfectly square to the subject, of the freshly chainsaw-cut end of a large bigleaf maple limb about eighteen inches across, lying on the forest floor. The sawn face is startlingly pale — cream and warm bone-white sapwood with faint growth rings — crossed by fine parallel chainsaw kerf marks radiating from one edge, with a fringe of pale damp sawdust caught on the lower rim. An irregular decay column, wet coffee-black and slightly fibrous and stringy, occupies roughly a third of the section and sits noticeably OFF-CENTRE toward the upper right. The bark ring around the pale face is soaked black and hung with grey-green foliose lichen and a thread of moss. Light: soft flat overcast, no direct sun and no flash, so the pale wood is by far the brightest thing in the frame and the surrounding forest floor falls to near black. Lens: 85mm macro at f/8, the entire cut face critically sharp edge to edge. Framing: 4:5, the cut face filling about eighty percent of the frame, dead centre, only a narrow dark border of ground around it. Palette: cream and bone at the centre, near-black surround, one thread of green. Mood: evidentiary, clinical, the interior revealed. No hands, no tools, no text, no logos, no watermark.

rol: Sección 4 'THE EAST WIND' — el hielo como PESO físico, no como postal. Es la prueba visual del argumento del Gorge.
prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of freezing rain glazing a bare deciduous branch. A continuous clear ice sheath about a quarter inch thick completely encases the twigs and the dormant buds, with small icicles forming and hanging from the underside, and the whole branch is visibly bent and sagging under the load. Behind it, a completely out-of-focus black-green wall of wet conifer. Light: dim, coming low and raking from a leaden east sky, so the ice reads as real glass with tiny internal refractions, a few hard cold specular points and no warmth anywhere in the frame. Lens: 100mm macro at f/2.8, very shallow depth of field, focus on the ice over the buds. Framing: horizontal 16:9, the branch entering from the left and sagging diagonally across the lower third, large dark empty space upper right. Palette: near-black background, neutral glassy highlights, absolutely no warm tone. Mood: quiet, physical, dangerous weight. No text, no people, no logos, no watermark.

rol: Sección 4 — el despacho de tormenta 24 h de noviembre a marzo. El único momento cálido de toda la página, y por eso mismo mide la urgencia.
prompt: Photorealistic documentary photograph, night, heavy rain, a residential Portland street. A large fallen tree limb lies diagonally across a wooden fence and the rear quarter of a parked car. The only light comes from vehicle headlights and an amber rotating beacon just out of frame. Two crew members in hi-vis yellow-green rain jackets with silver reflective bands are seen entirely from behind, one holding a chainsaw down at rest; rain streaks visibly through the headlight beam and the wet asphalt reflects the amber and the hi-vis in long smears. Light: mixed — warm 3200K headlight and amber beacon against a cold dark blue-green night, hard shadows, deep unlit areas. Lens: 35mm at f/2, 1/60 second, visible rain streaks and a few droplets on the front element. Framing: horizontal 16:9, the fallen limb as the dominant diagonal, the crew small in the middle distance. Palette: black-green night, amber, one hi-vis note. Mood: two in the morning, competent, unglamorous, no heroics. No faces, no readable text or lettering on any vehicle, no logos, no licence plates, no watermark.

rol: Sección 7 (FAQ) — ilustra una pregunta concreta y muy portlandina: 'Is the moss killing my tree?'. No es empapelado: es la prueba de una afirmación.
alt_original: Detailed close-up of textured tree bark with green and white lichen patterns.

rol: ⭐ EL HERO. Banda de foto ancha A SANGRE bajo el bloque de texto del fold, y también la og:image. Es la toma exacta que pidió Carlos: árbol de vereda, cables, casa detrás, camión con cesta. Tiene que decir «esto pasa en tu calle» antes que ninguna palabra.
prompt: Photorealistic documentary photograph of a residential street in Portland, Oregon in winter. Left of centre, a very large bare deciduous street tree grows out of the narrow grass planting strip between the curb and the sidewalk; its trunk is soaked dark and its bare limbs fill the upper half of the frame and pass directly through a run of overhead power and communication lines. Behind it, a 1920s craftsman house with a deep porch, painted clapboard siding and a wet shingle roof. At the right of frame, a white articulating bucket truck with its aerial lift boom raised up into the canopy and its outriggers down on the asphalt, a small pile of brush and wood chips beside it, orange traffic cones on the road. Parked cars along the curb, wet asphalt, a painted bike lane stripe. Light: flat even winter daylight, no direct sun and no drama; every surface is wet and dark and the sky is a featureless pale grey. Lens: 35mm at f/5.6 from across the street at standing height, level, no tilt. Framing: horizontal 16:9, the tree left of centre and the truck right, generous room around the trunk. Palette: black-green wet bark, grey asphalt, muted house paint, one small acid hi-vis note. Mood: an ordinary working Tuesday on a residential block. No faces, no readable text or lettering anywhere, no logos, no licence plates, no house numbers, no watermark.

rol: §2 «What's inside decides» — el SONDEO, que es el nombre del negocio y el servicio que vende. Urbano a propósito: el fondo desenfocado es un porche y un coche aparcado, no un bosque.
prompt: Photorealistic documentary close-up of a gloved hand swinging a white rubber sounding mallet against the trunk of a large street tree. The mallet head is in contact with the soaked dark bark; the forearm wears a hi-vis yellow-green sleeve with one silver retroreflective band; no face and no body beyond the forearm. The bark fills most of the frame, deeply fissured and wet, with a thin film of green algae in the crevices and one small patch of pale grey lichen. Behind the trunk, thrown completely out of focus, the porch and clapboard wall of a house, a parked car and a slice of grey street. Light: flat cold winter daylight, no direct sun, everything damp. Lens: 85mm at f/2.8, focus on the mallet head and the bark, background reduced to soft shapes. Framing: vertical 4:5, the trunk running the full height slightly left of centre, mallet and hand at mid-height. Palette: near-black wet bark, white rubber, one acid hi-vis note, muted grey-brown background. Mood: the first ten minutes of every job. No face, no text, no logos, no watermark.

rol: §3 «What we do» — la escala del trabajo Y la justificación del acento (el chaleco es lo único saturado). Sustituye a trepador-dosel.jpg, que era el mismo gesto en un parque sin ninguna señal de barrio.
prompt: Photorealistic documentary photograph looking up from the sidewalk of a residential street. A single climbing arborist is about thirty feet up in a bare winter street tree, seen from below and from behind so no face is visible, wearing a hi-vis yellow-green jacket with silver retroreflective bands, working on a climbing rope running through a friction saver over the limb above him. Behind and below him: the wet shingle roof, gutter and brick chimney of a two-storey house, overhead power lines crossing the frame, and the roof of a parked car at the bottom edge. The tree is leafless, its bark soaked dark, moss on the upper sides of the limbs. Light: flat cold winter daylight, the sky a dull pale grey between the branches. Lens: 50mm at f/4 from the sidewalk, the climber critically sharp, the house softly out of focus. Framing: vertical 3:4, the climber at the upper-third intersection, house and wires filling the rest. Palette: near-black wet bark, grey roof and sky, one acid hi-vis note. Mood: competent, unglamorous, unmistakably in a neighbourhood and not in a forest. No face, no text, no logos, no house numbers, no licence plates, no watermark.

rol: §3 — el ENTREGABLE. El informe escrito sobre el capó de la camioneta: la toma que Carlos pidió y la que convierte «evaluación» en un objeto que el cliente recibe.
prompt: Photorealistic documentary photograph, shot from above and slightly to one side, of a written tree assessment lying on the wet hood of a dark pickup truck parked on a residential street. On an aluminium clipboard: two pages of a printed report with a hand-drawn sketch of a tree in the margin and handwriting in carpenter pencil, the writing deliberately soft and illegible. Beside it on the hood: a white rubber sounding mallet with a hickory handle, a steel diameter tape, a folding rule, and a pair of worn leather work gloves. A forearm in a hi-vis sleeve enters from the right edge; no face and no body. The truck's wet paint reflects the bare branches overhead and a slice of pale sky. Light: flat cold winter daylight, water beaded on the paint. Lens: 50mm at f/5.6 at a slight angle, the far edge of the hood falling softly out of focus. Framing: horizontal 3:2, the clipboard filling the left two thirds. Palette: white paper, black wet paint, warm hickory, one acid hi-vis note. Mood: the paperwork is the product. No faces, no readable text or letterforms of any kind, no logos, no watermark.

rol: §6 «The streets we know» — la franja entre calzada y acera, que es literalmente el sitio donde crece el árbol de calle. Da el plano ancho del barrio que la página no tenía.
prompt: Photorealistic documentary photograph looking straight down a residential street in winter, camera standing in the middle of the road. On both sides, a continuous row of large bare street trees planted in the narrow grass strip between the curb and the sidewalk, their trunks lining up in perspective and their bare crowns meeting overhead into a tunnel. Wet asphalt, parked cars at the curb, wooden porches and clapboard houses set back behind, overhead power lines running along one side only. Light: flat cold winter daylight, the sky a dull pale grey through the branches. Lens: 35mm at f/8, level and centred, strong one-point perspective. Framing: horizontal 16:9. Palette: wet black bark, grey road, muted paint, a little green in the planting strip. Mood: an old neighbourhood that somebody planted on purpose a hundred years ago. No people, no faces, no readable text, no logos, no licence plates, no house numbers, no watermark.

rol: §6 — la acera levantada por raíces, la toma que Carlos pidió. Es la conversación comercial más frecuente del rubro («me dijeron que hay que quitar el árbol») convertida en imagen.
prompt: Photorealistic documentary photograph, low angle close to the ground, of a concrete sidewalk slab in a residential neighbourhood that has been lifted, tilted and cracked by the buttress root of a large street tree. The root is visible where it has broken out through the seam, wet and dark; the slab edge stands proud by about three inches and the crack runs diagonally across the panel. Behind: the narrow grass planting strip, the curb, wet asphalt, the base of the tree trunk and, out of focus, a picket fence and the porch of a house. A yellow folding rule lies across the lifted edge to give scale. Light: flat even winter daylight, wet concrete, no direct sun. Lens: 28mm at f/8, camera about eight inches off the ground, deep focus front to back. Framing: horizontal 3:2, the lifted slab edge running from lower-left to centre-right. Palette: grey concrete, black wet root, muted green grass. Mood: forensic, a problem you can trip on. No people, no text, no logos, no house numbers, no watermark.
